recipesPage.title: A little cardamom. A lot of magic.
recipesPage.description: From slow-simmered chai to celebration-worthy sweets, find thoughtful recipes that let cardamom shine.
recipesPage.heroImageAlt: A warm cup of chai with a teapot and spices on a table

recipes.title: Cardamom Rasmalai by Shimi’s Kitchen
recipes.excerpt: Soft chenna rounds steeped in saffron milk, finished with freshly crushed cardamom and pistachio.
recipes.imageAlt: A creamy Indian-inspired dessert topped with soft cream
ingredients: 2 tablespoons lemon juice, mixed with 2 tablespoons water
steps: Bring 750 ml of the milk to a gentle boil. Turn off the heat, add the diluted lemon juice a little at a time, and stir until the curds separate.
Strain the curds through a clean muslin cloth. Rinse briefly with cool water, then hang for 25 minutes so the chenna is moist but not dripping.
Knead the chenna until smooth and supple. Divide into 8 portions and shape into small, even discs.
Boil the sugar with 4 cups of water. Add the discs, cover, and cook at a lively simmer for 12 minutes. Let them cool in the syrup.
Warm the remaining milk with saffron and crushed cardamom. Simmer until lightly reduced, then cool.
Gently squeeze excess syrup from each disc and place them in the saffron milk. Chill for at least 2 hours and finish with pistachios.
recipes.tip: Crush the cardamom just before warming the milk; the fragrance stays brighter.

recipes.title: Elaichi Milk Tea by Shimi’s Kitchen
recipes.excerpt: A familiar cup made more memorable with freshly cracked green cardamom and a patient simmer.
recipes.imageAlt: A freshly brewed cup of chai with spices
ingredients: 1 to 2 teaspoons sugar, or to taste
steps: Bring the water and crushed cardamom to a gentle boil for 2 minutes.
Add the tea leaves and simmer for 1 minute, until the water turns a deep amber.
Pour in the milk and add sugar. Bring back to a gentle simmer, watching carefully so the tea does not boil over.
Strain into warm cups and serve straight away.
recipes.tip: For a stronger cup, steep the tea leaves a little longer before adding milk.
recipes.imageTitle: Elaichi Milk Tea by Shimi’s Kitchen

recipes.title: Elaichi Payasam By Shimi’s Kitchen
recipes.excerpt: A gently reduced milk pudding with tender rice, golden nuts and the delicate warmth of cardamom.
recipes.imageAlt: A creamy dessert served with a festive finish
ingredients: ¼ cup basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
⅓ cup sugar, or to taste
steps: Warm the ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and toast the cashews and raisins until golden. Set aside.
Drain the rice. Bring the milk to a gentle simmer in the same pan, then add the rice.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is soft and the milk has thickened.
Stir in the sugar, crushed cardamom and saffron. Simmer for another 3 minutes.
Fold in the toasted nuts. Serve warm, or chill and serve cold.
recipes.tip: Stir along the base of the pan often so the milk reduces evenly.

recipes.title: Cardamom Pistachio Latte by Shimi’s Kitchen
recipes.excerpt: Espresso, velvety milk and pistachio meet a subtle, fragrant note of freshly ground elaichi.
recipes.imageAlt: Fresh green cardamom pods and whole spices
ingredients: 1 double shot espresso or ½ cup strong coffee
¾ cup milk of your choice
1 tablespoon pistachio cream or pistachio syrup
A small pinch of freshly ground cardamom
steps: Warm the milk gently with pistachio cream, stirring until smooth. Do not let it boil.
Brew the espresso into a mug and stir in the cardamom.
Pour the pistachio milk over the espresso and finish with crushed pistachios.
recipes.tip: If your pistachio cream is sweetened, taste before adding anything extra.
recipes.imageTitle: Cardamom Pistachio Latte by Shimi’s Kitchen

localRecipes.title: Sunday Cardamom Chicken Biryani
localRecipes.excerpt: Layered basmati, tender chicken and whole spices come together in a fragrant, family-style dum.
localRecipes.imageAlt: A bowl of chicken biryani with basmati rice and herbs
ingredients: 300 g basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
5 green cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick and 4 cloves
A pinch of saffron soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
steps: Mix the chicken with yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste and salt. Leave to marinate while you prepare the rice.
Fry the onions in ghee until golden. Set aside half for layering. Add the whole spices to the pan, then add the marinated chicken and cook for 12 minutes.
Boil the rice in salted water until it is about 70 percent cooked. Drain well.
Spread half the rice over the chicken. Add herbs and some fried onions, then layer the remaining rice on top.
Drizzle the saffron milk over the rice. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently from the sides and bring the layers to the table.
localRecipes.tip: Keep the cardamom pods whole so they perfume the rice without overpowering it.

localRecipes.title: Coconut & Cardamom Ladoo
localRecipes.excerpt: A quick festive sweet with toasted coconut, gentle sweetness and a bright finish of elaichi.
localRecipes.imageAlt: Traditional Indian sweets arranged for a festive table
ingredients: 2 cups unsweetened desiccated coconut, plus extra for rolling
steps: Warm a wide pan over low heat. Toast the coconut for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the condensed milk and cardamom. Stir continuously until the mixture thickens and begins to pull away from the pan.
Fold in the cashews if using. Let the mixture cool until comfortable to handle.
Grease your palms lightly and roll into small balls. Coat with extra coconut and leave to set for 15 minutes.
localRecipes.tip: Keep the heat low; coconut can turn from fragrant to toasted very quickly.

localRecipes.title: Cardamom Pistachio Iced Coffee
localRecipes.excerpt: A cool, creamy coffee with a whisper of cardamom and a nutty pistachio finish.
localRecipes.imageAlt: Green cardamom pods and whole spices on a dark surface
ingredients: 1 double shot of espresso or ½ cup strong chilled coffee
1 tablespoon pistachio syrup or pistachio cream
A pinch of freshly ground cardamom
Ice and crushed pistachios to finish
steps: Stir the espresso with pistachio syrup and a small pinch of cardamom.
Fill a tall glass with ice and pour in the cold milk.
Slowly pour the coffee mixture over the milk. Finish with crushed pistachios and serve.
localRecipes.tip: Start with only a pinch of cardamom; its citrusy aroma is lovely when kept subtle.
